codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured refactoring of SubprocessTransport to be engine-aware. The implementation correctly uses the engine registry for command building, handles engine-specific output parsing (NDJSON for OpenCode, plain text for Claude), wires config.dispatcher.model through resolveModels() to the CLI --model flag, and checks binary availability in the constructor. Auto-detect routing is correct: Claude → CLI only, OpenCode → SDK then CLI. Both flywheel-shell.tsx code paths (initial start and resume) are updated. 27 tests provide good coverage of all validation contract items. No blocking issues found.

issues.description: VAL-DISP-008 test uses 'nonexistent-engine' which throws from getEngine() in the registry ('Unknown engine') rather than from the Bun.which() binary-not-found check. The test validates that an unknown engine name errors, but does not actually exercise the Bun.which() code path that produces the 'CLI not found — install it with...' error message. The Bun.which() code IS present in the constructor (line ~82 of subprocess-transport.ts), so the behavior is implemented — just the specific binary-not-found error path isn't tested. Mocking Bun.which() would be needed to properly test this.

For OpenCode, the systemPrompt passed to buildDispatcherCommand() via options.systemPrompt is silently ignored by the OpenCode provider's buildDispatcherCommand() — it only uses options.model and options.prompt. The system prompt is instead manually concatenated into stdinContent on line 121. This works correctly but creates an implicit contract: the SubprocessTransport must know that OpenCode needs system prompt in stdin while Claude gets it via --system-prompt flag. The EngineCommand.stdinPrompt boolean partially signals this, but the system prompt concatenation is transport-level logic rather than engine-level.

The resume path uses a dynamic import for resolveModels: `const { resolveModels } = await import('../../config/loader')`. The initial start path (line 607) also uses a dynamic import. This is fine functionally, but the initial start path at the top of the file already has a static import of autoDetectTransport — it's slightly inconsistent that resolveModels uses dynamic import while autoDetectTransport is static. Not a bug, just a style note.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The OpenCode buildDispatcherCommand() silently ignores the systemPrompt parameter from DispatcherCommandOptions. The SubprocessTransport compensates by manually concatenating the system prompt into stdinContent for OpenCode. This implicit behavior should be documented somewhere — either in the DispatcherCommandOptions type comment or in a convention about how engines handle system prompts differently. Currently nothing in AGENTS.md or the type definitions warns future developers that OpenCode's dispatcher command builder ignores systemPrompt.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/engines/providers/opencode/index.ts:88-101 — buildDispatcherCommand() receives options.systemPrompt but never uses it. src/dispatcher/subprocess-transport.ts:120-121 — stdinContent manually includes systemPrompt for stdinPrompt=true engines.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The architecture.md library doc describes the pre-optimization state ('Currently (pre-optimization), the transports bypass the engine registry entirely'). Now that the dispatcher transport has been refactored to be engine-aware, this library entry is slightly stale. The evaluator transport still hardcodes opencode so the statement is partially true, but the 'currently' framing is no longer accurate for the dispatcher path.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/architecture.md — 'Currently (pre-optimization), the transports bypass the engine registry entirely and hardcode opencode run --format json.' This is no longer true for the dispatcher transport after commit 6dab3c0.

summary: PASS. The dispatcher SubprocessTransport refactoring is well-implemented. All 4 modified files (subprocess-transport.ts, auto-detect.ts, flywheel-shell.tsx, test file) are consistent and correct. The engine registry is properly used for command building, config.dispatcher.model flows through resolveModels() to the --model CLI flag, auto-detect routing correctly sends Claude to CLI-only and OpenCode to SDK-then-CLI, and output parsing handles both NDJSON and plain text formats. Three non-blocking issues identified: (1) the binary-not-found test exercises the wrong error path (registry lookup vs Bun.which), (2) OpenCode's buildDispatcherCommand silently ignores systemPrompt, and (3) minor import style inconsistency. None of these affect correctness or user-facing behavior.
